giant-wordmark.definition: The family name set as large as the viewport allows on a flat field, little else; may mix styles letter by letter to show range.
giant-wordmark.cues: one dominant name, flat colour, minimal copy

sentence-as-specimen.definition: A headline sentence about the font, set in the font (sometimes beside one oversized glyph or rotating through styles): the pitch is the specimen.
sentence-as-specimen.cues: readable claim or announcement in display size, CTA nearby

typeset-page.definition: A classical typeset composition (title page, broadside, dictionary entry) that uses the family's own hierarchy, italics and ornaments.
typeset-page.cues: centred stacks, rules, ornaments, multiple sizes and italics

kinetic-type.definition: The type in motion is the hero: animated, 3D, generative, video clips, or axes driven by scroll.
kinetic-type.cues: canvas/video/WebGL, scroll-scrubbed variation, the capture looks mid-animation

interactive-specimen.definition: The hero is a specimen the visitor manipulates straight away (axes, weight, contrast, text), via controls or the wheel.
interactive-specimen.cues: sliders, toggles or editable text inside the first screen

construction-drawing.definition: A glyph shown as its construction (Bézier points, skeleton, strokes), often drawn on.
construction-drawing.cues: outline points, handles, metric lines in the hero

name-over-photo.definition: Name and a short line over a full-bleed mood photograph.
name-over-photo.cues: landscape or scene photo, type overlaid

material-photo.definition: A photograph of physical material (paper, textile, objects) carrying or framing the type.
material-photo.cues: tactile still life, the type printed or knitted on the material

illustration-scene.definition: An illustrated scene or mascot staged with the type; the illustration sets the tone.

prop-collage.definition: A collage of designed artefacts (documents, tickets, packaging, diagrams) set in the font, implying a fictional world.
prop-collage.cues: many small designed objects, all set in the font

product-landing.definition: The software-product landing pattern: headline, tagline, paragraph, primary and secondary buttons.
product-landing.cues: SaaS layout, 'Try it now' and 'GitHub' buttons, common for coding fonts

title-sequence.definition: Full-screen frames revealing name, facts and specimen in sequence, often skippable.

origin-reference.definition: The source or inspiration (historical artefact, technology, place, genre history) explained in prose and shown visually.

essay.definition: Long-form first-person or editorial text (designer essay, process chapters, commissioner's foreword), laid out like an article.

making-of.definition: The process shown visually: sketches, proofs, iterations, photos of the designer at work.
making-of.cues: process images with little text, stages

design-brief.definition: The problem the font solves (purpose, readers, constraints, principles) stated as a list or spec.

large-text-intro.definition: A short 'about' paragraph set large in the font, so the description doubles as a text specimen.
large-text-intro.cues: one big paragraph near the top

article-teaser.definition: A short teaser and a link to an off-page article or interview about the making.

scroll-narrative.definition: A pinned, scroll-driven sequence telling a concept metaphor through animated type and diagrams.

self-test-evidence.definition: The design rationale backed by a small test the visitor runs on themselves (reading speed, legibility).
self-test-evidence.cues: a quiz or timer next to research prose

designer-bio.definition: A short, informal bio of the designer with contact links.

full-grid.definition: The whole character set in uniform cells, in encoding order (sometimes with key labels for dingbat fonts).

glyph-inspector.definition: A grid plus a large preview of the selected or hovered glyph on its metric lines.
glyph-inspector.cues: big glyph panel, cap-height and x-height lines

category-lines.definition: The set typeset as running lines per category (or one moving line), no cells.
category-lines.cues: A–Z, a–z, 0–9 as lines of text

category-tabs.definition: Tabs or a dropdown switch a large-size strip of one category at a time.

bento-cards.definition: A grid of cards, each a slice of the set or one feature (arrows, numerals, ligatures).

keymap-grid.definition: Pictogram or dingbat cells labelled with the key that types them.
keymap-grid.cues: key letter in each cell corner

per-row-controls.definition: Several sample rows, each with its own style, size and leading controls.
per-row-controls.cues: a control strip on every row

global-toolbar.definition: One persistent toolbar restyles all editable samples on the page.
global-toolbar.cues: sticky bar of selects and sliders

labelled-editable-lines.definition: Each style gets a small label and editable lines at a fitting size; click to type, no toolbar.
labelled-editable-lines.cues: contenteditable lines, style labels, no controls

slider-sandbox.definition: One editable sample with a few axis and size sliders around it.

feature-toggle-board.definition: One big sample line plus a panel of OpenType feature toggles labelled with their tags.

in-context-editable.definition: A realistic layout (classifieds, menu, poster) whose text is editable.
in-context-editable.cues: editable text inside a designed artefact

code-playground.definition: A mock code editor with language tabs and themes, set in the (coding) font, with font controls.

creative-toy.definition: A playful maker that turns the font into a composition: patterns, shareable images, style pairings, word-by-word styling.
creative-toy.cues: share or download buttons, presets, unusual gestures

word-stack.definition: Display words or phrases stacked vertically, often cropped, for rhythm and character.

in-use-mockups.definition: Realistic applications (posters, books, screens, signage, client work) as a wall, carousel, shuffler or filmed object.

prop-collage.definition: Invented artefacts (UI windows, tickets, files, stickers) set in the font, collaged into a scene.

poster-series.definition: A sequence of self-contained poster or specimen-page compositions, often pastiching a period.
poster-series.cues: full-width graphic panels one after another

editorial-in-use.definition: The font running a real or realistic publication (articles, magazine pages) with genuine content.

kinetic-scenes.definition: Animated, generative or physics compositions (falling or scattered glyphs, liquid) after the hero.

use-case-samples.definition: Tabs or panels with realistic content samples per use case (code, data tables, UI).

modular-grid.definition: A uniform grid of cells mixing large glyphs, sentences and notes, like a specimen sheet.

themed-infographic.definition: An interactive infographic on the font's theme, set in the font so the numerals and labels do real work.

style-word-grid.definition: Every style named and shown on a sample word or the same paragraph.
style-word-grid.cues: style labels plus samples in a grid or stack

designspace-map.definition: The family laid out along its axes: a matrix, a cube, or clickable stops that set the sample.
designspace-map.cues: width × weight table, axis cube, stop pickers

big-number-stats.definition: The family's size stated as huge figures (glyphs, weights, styles).

feature-before-after.definition: A feature or alternate shown off vs on (side by side, overlaid, toggled or typed in a loop) with a short explanation.

feature-index.definition: Every stylistic set or ligature group catalogued as cards or tiles (input → output), often toggleable or exportable as settings.

axis-explainer.definition: Each variable axis demonstrated on its own: a word plus slider, labelled steps, or animation fitting frames.
axis-explainer.cues: axis names, steps, one axis at a time

annotated-specimen.definition: Letterforms with technical annotations or numbered figures (measurements, ink traps, angles), one decision per row.

system-diagrams.definition: The family's logic (weight curve, optical sizes, widths) explained with charts, like a design-system manual.

design-notes.definition: A sequence of design decisions, each with a visual and a short caption, as a carousel or video tiles.
design-notes.cues: slides or looping tiles per topic

multiscript-specimen.definition: Sample lines in several scripts, each tagged with script and settings.

diacritic-word-wall.definition: Real words from many languages chosen for their diacritics, at display size.

coverage-statement.definition: A big-type sentence stating the coverage instead of showing it.

versus-tabs.definition: Tabs pick a rival typeface; the same text is set in both, stacked.

quote-columns.definition: User quotes set in the font, in plain columns.

embedded-social-posts.definition: Embedded posts from users, with avatars and handles.

on-page-cart.definition: Buying happens on the page: licence picker, packages and prices, preview, add to cart.

link-out-cta.definition: Prominent buy, trial or download buttons linking to an external shop or repository.

free-download.definition: A free download with a plain-language licence summary and/or developer install instructions.
free-download.cues: OFL, npm or brew commands, press kit

build-configurator.definition: Options (alternates, spacing, ligatures) select which pre-built files you download.
build-configurator.cues: option toggles plus a download button

credits-colophon.definition: Credits: designers, contributors, testers, tools, fonts used.

big-sign-off.definition: A large closing statement, then small legal lines.

personal-sign-off.definition: An informal closing note from the designer.

slim-legal-bar.definition: One or two lines: copyright and credit.

related-projects.definition: Cards linking to the designer's or foundry's other fonts.

keyboard-driven-app.definition: A single-screen app driven by keyboard shortcuts.

desktop-os-windows.definition: The site staged as a desktop OS with draggable windows.

arcade-leaderboard.definition: A browser game with a high-score table and font prizes.

scroll-door-animation.definition: A pinned, scroll-scrubbed illustration opening like doors.

announcement-banner.definition: A thin site-wide banner (donation, launch, sale).

masthead-nav.definition: A slim header with name, tagline and section tabs, standing in for a hero.
